purpose: Engineer token budgets, layered digests, compaction triggers, and context-rot measurement so long-running multi-agent work keeps invariants and working set while freeing capacity safely.
assumptions: Model context is finite and meterable with a known tokenizer
Some strings are character-critical and must not be paraphrased
Bulk artifacts can be stored outside the prompt with durable locators
exclusions: End-user product analytics unrelated to agent context
Storing secrets in prompts or telemetry

competency_questions.question: What is the current token ledger by segment and headroom to hard cap?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: lists tokens for system/tools/working_set/history/retrieved and remaining headroom

competency_questions.question: Which compaction triggers are active and what action should fire now?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states util% or rot trigger and next action compact|externalize|refuse

competency_questions.question: What belongs in the active working set and pinned fact register for this task?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names goal, active paths, open decisions, and key task KV facts

competency_questions.question: Which strings are never-compact invariants and where are they placed in the prompt?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: lists pin set and positions (system/tail) not mid-digest only

competency_questions.question: How is recent history separated from layered digests?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states tail policy and at least L0 vs L1/L2 roles

competency_questions.question: What is kept verbatim vs summarized when compressing narrative?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives class table with sha/path/error vs narrative examples

competency_questions.question: What should be externalized vs dropped under budget pressure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names at least one externalize candidate with locator need and one drop class

competency_questions.question: How do you rehydrate a detail that left the prompt?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives locator or layer-descent steps with a size cap

competency_questions.question: How is context rot measured before and after compaction?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: describes probe set and when scores are recorded

competency_questions.question: Does compression fidelity meet the floor given position bias?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: reports ratio and probe score and pin placement check

competency_questions.question: Why is bare sliding window unsafe and what is the emergency alternative?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names dropped-invariant risk and re-pin + structured eviction alternative

competency_questions.question: How should multi-agent spawns share budget without cloning full transcripts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: specifies task packet contents, role caps, and digest return schema

glossary.definition: Maximum input tokens allowed for a model call; local preflight must enforce
Minimal high-fidelity live task state required for the next correct action
Lowest digest layer: short bullet facts with ids, paths, decisions
Degradation where model stops honoring earlier constraints or settled facts
Substring that must not be paraphrased (SHA, path, error, threshold)
Move bulk artifact out of prompt; leave locator+hash+gist
Demand-driven reload of detail from store or deeper digest layer
Priority sequence for freeing tokens under pressure
Lean spawn payload for a subagent: pins + goal + scoped files, not full chat
Minimum probe score that outranks compression ratio targets

nodes.definition: Maintain an explicit token ledger for system, tools, retrieved docs, working set, and history. A context window is a hard capacity (e.g. 128k–1M tokens depending on model); without a ledger, compaction decisions are guesswork and overflow truncates the wrong segments. Count input tokens with the same tokenizer the model uses; treat tool JSON and code blocks as high-density cost centers (often 1.2–2× prose tokens per character-visible length).

base.update_signal: measured input tokens exceed planned budget by >10% or overflow truncates mid-artifact

pros.claim: Explicit ledger makes eviction and compaction falsifiable
pros.example: at 90% of hard cap, remaining 10% reserved for reply + tool returns

cons.claim: Ledger lag of one turn can still overflow on large tool payloads
cons.example: a 40k-token tool dump bypasses a stale budget snapshot

failure_modes: counting characters as tokens (off by 2–4× on code)
acceptance_tests: budget report lists tokens for system, tools, working_set, history, retrieved with sum ≤ hard_cap

nodes.definition: Define the minimal live task state that must remain high-fidelity: current goal, open decisions, active file paths, failing tests, and the last accepted plan step. Working set is not 'everything recent' — it is the set without which the next action cannot be correct. Typical target: 8–20% of usable budget for long multi-agent runs; grow only when the active task surface expands.

base.update_signal: agent re-asks for already-stated goal or reopens closed decisions after a compaction

pros.claim: Preserving working set prevents goal drift after compaction
pros.example: after 3 compact cycles goal string still matches task header

cons.claim: Over-wide working set starves history and retrieval slots
cons.example: working set at 45% of budget forces aggressive history loss

failure_modes: equating working set with entire conversation tail
dropping failing-test names while keeping chat niceties
acceptance_tests: working set artifact names goal, active paths, open decisions, last plan step

nodes.definition: Identify strings and structures that must never be summarized away: safety rules, hard denials, ASSIGNEE/scope constraints, acceptance criteria, and authenticated task headers. Invariants are pinned verbatim; digests may reference them by id but must not paraphrase obligations. Pin cost is intentional: 2–8k tokens of invariants is cheaper than a single out-of-scope force-push.

base.update_signal: a compacted prompt loses a hard denial or changes ASSIGNEE/scope meaning

pros.claim: Verbatim pins eliminate obligation drift under compression
pros.example: HARD DENIALS block still byte-stable across 5 compactions

cons.claim: Pin bloat reduces room for task-specific detail
cons.example: 12k pinned boilerplate on a 32k model leaves little working set

failure_modes: summarizing 'do not force-push' into 'be careful with git'
acceptance_tests: invariant set listed; each item marked pin=verbatim; none appear only inside digests
revisit_triggers: new hard denial added by integrator

nodes.definition: Keep a short high-fidelity tail of the most recent turns (often last 2–6 exchanges or ~5–15% of budget) because recency bias and repair of the latest error both depend on unsummarized detail. Older turns graduate into digests; the tail is the only place mid-repair state is trustworthy.

base.update_signal: agent repeats a just-failed approach that was only in the dropped last turn

pros.claim: Tail preserves repair context for the active failure
pros.example: retry uses the exact error string from last tool call

cons.claim: Long tails with huge tool dumps dominate budget
cons.example: single 30k stack trace in tail forces digest of all prior work

failure_modes: dropping the failing tool output while keeping user chit-chat
acceptance_tests: tail policy states N turns or token cap and lists what graduates to digest

nodes.definition: Maintain layered digests: L0 bullet facts (≤500 tokens), L1 section summaries (1–3k), L2 episode narratives (3–8k). Higher layers cite lower layer ids. Compaction promotes detail upward only after L0 facts are extracted; never jump from raw log to a single vague paragraph. Hierarchy enables selective rehydration of one episode without reloading the whole history.

base.update_signal: post-compaction answers miss concrete ids/paths that existed only in raw history

pros.claim: Layered digests preserve queryable facts under tight budgets
pros.example: L0 still lists failing test name after L2 narrative compresses story

cons.claim: Poor promotion drops numbers and paths at L0
cons.example: L0 says 'fixed tests' without naming which tests

failure_modes: one-shot summarize entire history to 200 tokens
layers without stable ids so rehydration cannot target
acceptance_tests: at least two digest layers present with L0 containing concrete ids/paths/decisions
revisit_triggers: rehydration often fails to find detail

nodes.definition: Decide what stays verbatim: error messages, SHAs, file paths, numeric thresholds, protocol headers, failing assertions, and legal/safety clauses. Verbatim spans are short and high-value; they are carved out before summarization. Rule of thumb: if a single wrong character changes action (SHA, path, exit code), keep verbatim.

base.update_signal: compacted context rewrites a commit SHA or filepath and agent acts on wrong target

pros.claim: Character-critical tokens survive compression
pros.example: DELIVERED-SHA remains exact hex after digest

cons.claim: Over-verbatim keeps noise (full stack frames) that should be clipped
cons.example: keeping 200-line stack instead of top frame + type

acceptance_tests: verbatim policy lists classes: sha, path, error, numeric threshold, protocol header

nodes.definition: Separate summarize-worthy narrative (why a decision was made, alternatives rejected) from droppable chatter (acknowledgements, duplicate tool noise). Summarize when future decisions need the why; drop when only the outcome matters and is already in L0. Target compression: narrative 5–15×; never compress below the point where rejected alternatives disappear if still relevant.

base.update_signal: agent re-proposes an already-rejected alternative that was only in dropped narrative

pros.claim: Policy prevents silent loss of rejected paths
pros.example: digest notes 'avoided force-push per hard denial'

cons.claim: Over-summarizing collapses distinct failures into one vague 'had issues'
cons.example: three distinct gate failures become one sentence

failure_modes: summarizing and dropping the same class without criterion
keeping all tool stdout 'just in case'
acceptance_tests: policy table: keep_verbatim | summarize | externalize | drop with examples per class

nodes.definition: Move bulky recoverable artifacts out of the prompt into repo files, object stores, or ticket attachments; leave a locator + hash + one-line gist in context. Externalization is preferred over lossy summary when the artifact may need exact re-read (logs, full diffs, large JSON). Locator must be actionable (path, URL, blob id) and freshness-stamped.

base.update_signal: agent cannot re-open a log that was 'summarized away' with no locator

pros.claim: Exact artifacts remain recoverable without prompt bloat
pros.example: 1-line pointer replaces 25k log; rehydrate on demand

cons.claim: Broken locators or deleted files create false confidence
cons.example: gist says 'see /tmp/log' after temp cleaned

acceptance_tests: each externalized item has locator, content hash or mtime, and 1-line gist in context
revisit_triggers: /tmp or ephemeral paths used as locators

nodes.definition: Define objective triggers to compact: utilization ≥80–90% of hard cap; projected next tool return would exceed remaining headroom; turn count since last compact ≥K; or measured context-rot score crosses threshold. Avoid compaction every turn (cost and churn) and avoid waiting for hard failure. Triggers should be measurable from the token ledger and task telemetry.

base.update_signal: session hits hard overflow without a prior compact attempt

pros.claim: Objective triggers make compaction ops-reviewable
pros.example: compact fires at 85% util before overflow

cons.claim: Too-low thresholds thrash and lose nuance
cons.example: compact every 2 turns at 50% util

acceptance_tests: written thresholds: util%, projected headroom, max turns since compact

nodes.definition: Detect context rot: the model stops using early constraints, contradicts prior decisions, or re-asks settled facts. Proxies: constraint-recall probes (quiz on pinned rules), decision consistency checks, and attention to ids from L0. Rot is not just length — a clean 20k context can outperform a noisy 100k one. Measure before/after compaction with the same probe set.

base.update_signal: probe fails on ASSIGNEE or scope after session lengthens even under budget

pros.claim: Rot metrics justify compaction quality not just size
pros.example: post-compact probe ≥ pre-compact on invariants

cons.claim: Probes add cost and can themselves bloat context if naively inlined
cons.example: 20-question probe each turn costs 2k tokens

failure_modes: assuming longer context is always better
acceptance_tests: rot probe set defined; run at least at compact boundaries; scores recorded
revisit_triggers: accepted tasks later show constraint violations
probes always pass yet users report drift

nodes.definition: Before expensive tools or large retrieval, forecast token delta: expected tool return size (p50/p90 from history), prompt growth, and reply reserve (often 2–8k). If p90 return > remaining headroom after reserve, compact or externalize first. Forecast errors should update size priors.

base.update_signal: tool return regularly overflows despite 'enough room' gut feel

pros.claim: Forecast prevents mid-tool context death
pros.example: p90=25k tool blocked when headroom=12k; compact first

cons.claim: Priors wrong on new tools cause over-cautious delays
cons.example: new API always assumed 50k until observed

failure_modes: using p50 only when variance is high
acceptance_tests: before large tool: recorded headroom, p90 estimate, go/compact decision

nodes.definition: When forced to free tokens, evict in order: (1) duplicate tool noise, (2) old dropped-class chatter, (3) aged L2 narrative already covered by L0, (4) stale retrieval chunks, (5) older history tail beyond policy, never (6) system invariants or active working set. Document the order; reverse ad-hoc deletions cause silent goal loss.

base.update_signal: compaction drops working-set goal while keeping duplicate npm install logs

excluded: random truncation from the middle of the prompt

pros.claim: Stable eviction order protects high-value spans under pressure
pros.example: pins+working set untouched at 95% util

cons.claim: Rigid order may keep low-value L2 too long if L0 incomplete
cons.example: L2 retained while L0 missing SHAs

failure_modes: FIFO drop from the front including system
acceptance_tests: eviction order written; simulation on a full session shows pins retained
revisit_triggers: large protected set prevents any eviction

nodes.definition: Provide a path to pull detail back: from external store by locator, from L2→L1→raw if archived, or by re-running a bounded retrieval. Rehydration is demand-driven (answer a CQ or resume a subtask), not full session restore. Cap rehydrate size; prefer the smallest layer that answers.

base.update_signal: agent cannot recover detail needed for revise because only vague L2 remains

pros.claim: Selective rehydrate restores precision without full reload
pros.example: re-read one log path to fix SHA mismatch

cons.claim: Rehydrate loops can re-bloat context if not budgeted
cons.example: pulling 5 full files each turn

failure_modes: rehydrate entire history on any uncertainty
acceptance_tests: rehydrate procedure documented with size cap and stop condition

nodes.definition: Track achieved compression ratio vs fidelity probes. Aggressive 50× summaries often destroy numeric anchors; mild 3–8× on narrative with verbatim carve-outs usually preserves decision quality. Set a minimum fidelity floor (e.g. probe ≥0.85 on invariants) that overrides ratio goals.

base.update_signal: high compression celebrated while constraint probes drop below 0.7

excluded: BLEU against chat logs as sole quality

pros.claim: Fidelity floor stops unsafe over-compression
pros.example: block ship of digest if invariant probe <0.85

cons.claim: Over-strict floors prevent any compaction on small windows
cons.example: 32k model cannot move if floor demands 99% recall of all prose

acceptance_tests: report ratio and probe scores together for each compact event
revisit_triggers: ratio stuck near 1.0 with overflow risk

nodes.definition: Account for lost-in-the-middle and primacy/recency effects: critical constraints perform better at start (system) and end (tail), not buried mid-prompt. After compaction, re-place pins and working set at privileged positions; do not leave them only inside a middle digest blob.

base.update_signal: model ignores a rule that exists only mid-prompt in a 80k context

included: working set near end before user turn
excluded: internal transformer attention research without ops mapping

pros.claim: Position-aware layout recovers compliance without more tokens
pros.example: moving hard denials to system+tail cuts violations

cons.claim: Over-duplicating pins everywhere wastes budget
cons.example: same 3k rules pasted 4 times

failure_modes: burying ASSIGNEE only inside a long digest
assuming model reads all tokens equally
acceptance_tests: layout checklist: invariants in system; working set near tail; digest in middle

nodes.definition: Document why naive keep-last-N-tokens fails: it drops system invariants, loses early acceptance criteria, and severs dependency on early design decisions. Sliding window is acceptable only as a last-resort emergency after structured eviction fails — and must re-prepend pins.

base.update_signal: implementation uses drop-oldest without re-pinning system rules

pros.claim: Naming the anti-pattern prevents 'simple' overflow fixes that break safety
pros.example: code review blocks bare sliding window

cons.claim: Emergency window still needed under hard faults — must be paired with re-pin
cons.example: crash path forgets re-pin step

failure_modes: sliding window that clips system message
acceptance_tests: design doc forbids bare sliding window; emergency path includes re-pin invariants
revisit_triggers: any overflow handler adds FIFO drop

nodes.definition: Allocate budget across parent, subagents, and xverify roles: subagents should start lean (fresh context + task packet), not clone the full parent transcript. Shared pins can be a common prefix; task-specific bulk stays local. Parent retains orchestration state; workers return digests not full chains. Prevents N× replication of the same 50k history.

base.update_signal: each subagent receives full parent transcript and hits cap before working

pros.claim: Role-scoped budgets multiply effective capacity
pros.example: 3 subagents × 20k packets << 3×80k clones

cons.claim: Under-sharing causes duplicated retrieval and inconsistent facts
cons.example: each agent fetches different file versions

failure_modes: no budget for worker replies into parent
acceptance_tests: spawn policy: packet contents + token cap; parent merge expects digest schema

nodes.definition: Load detail only when a step needs it: start with L0 + goal, pull file bodies on edit, pull logs on failure. Progressive disclosure is the dual of eviction — an admit policy. Pair with forecast so disclosure cannot overrun headroom.

base.update_signal: agent preloads entire repo tree into context at task start

excluded: eager full-corpus RAG for every turn

pros.claim: Admit-only-as-needed keeps early turns cheap and focused
pros.example: first turn uses 8k not 80k

cons.claim: Too-lazy loading causes extra round-trips and partial edits
cons.example: edits file without reading current content

acceptance_tests: load policy: default L0; read-before-edit; logs on fail; cap per admit

nodes.definition: Emit structured telemetry per turn: tokens_in, tokens_by_segment, compact_events, probe_scores, evictions. Telemetry enables offline tuning of thresholds and proves gate-time claims about context discipline. Strip secrets; keep ids and sizes.

base.update_signal: cannot explain why an agent overflowed or dropped a constraint

pros.claim: Telemetry makes context engineering inspectable
pros.example: postmortem shows eviction of working set at t=41

cons.claim: Verbose telemetry can itself bloat if written into the prompt
cons.example: dumping 5k metrics into system each turn

acceptance_tests: telemetry schema includes tokens_by_segment and compact_reason; sample run produces records

nodes.definition: Enforce a hard cap in the runtime: refuse to send prompts over limit; prefer fail-closed with compact/externalize over silent provider truncation. Provider-side truncation is untrusted because it may drop system or tail unpredictably. Client-side enforcement is part of correctness.

base.update_signal: API returns truncated prompt or context_length_exceeded with no local pre-check

pros.claim: Local hard cap prevents undefined provider truncation
pros.example: preflight blocks send at 100% of model limit

cons.claim: Too-strict local estimator may refuse valid prompts if tokenizer mismatch
cons.example: estimate 5% high causes false refusals

failure_modes: rely on server error as the only control
acceptance_tests: preflight check exists; on fail runs compact/evict once then refuse with error

nodes.definition: Maintain a small register of durable task facts (branch name, task id, deliverable paths, gate commands) separate from narrative digests. Register entries are short key-value lines updated in place; they are the preferred L0 substrate for multi-hour work.

base.update_signal: agent invents a wrong branch name after narrative-only compaction

pros.claim: KV register survives when prose digests drift
pros.example: branch=grok/task-007-ctxeng always exact

cons.claim: Stale register entries mislead if not updated on task change
cons.example: old TASK-005 paths after new assign

acceptance_tests: register file or block with ≤30 keys; updated when task facts change

edges.why_related: workers return digests not full clones (causal ops link)
failed enforce must not FIFO-drop system
after eviction ensure rehydrate still works

edges.resolution_rule: carve character-critical spans first; summarize only non-verbatim narrative

edges.why_related: long high-fidelity tail vs room for structured digests
edges.resolution_rule: cap tail by tokens; graduate older turns to L0/L1 before growing tail

edges.why_related: share enough for consistency vs keep worker contexts lean
edges.resolution_rule: share pins+task packet only; workers do not clone full parent working set

edges.why_related: aggressive ratio targets vs probe fidelity
edges.resolution_rule: fidelity floor outranks ratio; stop compression when probes fail

conflict_axes.name: fidelity_vs_compression
conflict_axes.description: Preserve decision quality vs free tokens
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: enforce fidelity floor; compress narrative only after verbatim carve-outs

conflict_axes.name: tail_vs_digest_room
conflict_axes.description: Recent raw turns vs structured historical digests
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: token-cap the tail; graduate older turns on schedule

conflict_axes.name: pin_bloat_vs_safety
conflict_axes.description: More pinned rules vs remaining task capacity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pin only hard denials and acceptance criteria; KV register for task facts

conflict_axes.name: share_vs_isolate_agents
conflict_axes.description: Consistent shared state vs lean worker contexts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: share pins+packet; isolate bulk; merge digests

conflict_axes.name: eager_load_vs_progressive
conflict_axes.description: Preload context vs load on demand
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: progressive disclosure with read-before-edit and forecast gates

conflict_axes.name: externalize_vs_inline
conflict_axes.description: Pointers out of band vs everything in prompt
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: externalize when p90 size > headroom fraction; keep gist+hash inline

conflict_axes.name: trigger_sensitivity
conflict_axes.description: Early compact thrash vs late overflow
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: util 80–90% plus forecast; avoid every-turn compact

conflict_axes.name: position_duplication
conflict_axes.description: Duplicate pins for attention vs token cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: system + near-tail once each; no mid-prompt-only; avoid 4× paste

conflict_axes.name: emergency_window_vs_structure
conflict_axes.description: FIFO emergency drop vs ordered eviction
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: structured first; emergency window only with mandatory re-pin

edge_cases.description: Tool returns 40k JSON when headroom is 8k
edge_cases.trigger: p90 tool size unknown or underestimated
edge_cases.mitigation: preflight forecast; stream/truncate tool to store; gist+hash only in prompt

edge_cases.description: Provider silently truncates middle of prompt
edge_cases.trigger: no local hard cap; rely on API
edge_cases.mitigation: local token preflight; refuse or compact before send

edge_cases.description: Subagent spawned with full parent transcript
edge_cases.mitigation: task packet policy; cap worker budget; return digest

edge_cases.trigger: verbatim policy missing for hex ids
edge_cases.mitigation: carve SHAs; store in register; test with probe

edge_cases.description: Context rot with utilization only at 50%
edge_cases.trigger: noisy redundant tool logs dominate attention
edge_cases.mitigation: evict duplicates; re-place pins; measure probes not just size

edge_cases.description: Rehydrate locator points at deleted /tmp file
edge_cases.mitigation: use repo or durable store paths; include hash; fail loud on miss
split true invariants from task KV; trim style tips from pins
raise threshold; min turns between compacts; track thrash metric
ban bare FIFO; re-pin path mandatory
gate edits on file read; budget for read

workflow.description: Count tokens per segment with model tokenizer
Update goal, paths, open decisions, last plan step
Ensure hard denials and acceptance criteria present verbatim
Estimate p90 tool/retrieval growth + reply reserve
If thresholds hit, run ordered eviction and digest promotion
Extract SHAs paths errors before summarize
Promote narrative to L0/L1/L2 with ids
Write bulky artifacts out; leave locator+hash+gist
workflow.gate: each bulk item has durable locator

workflow.description: Run constraint-recall and decision consistency probes
Place pins in system and working set near tail
Log segment sizes, compact reasons, probes

dominance_rules.rationale: undefined truncation is worse than delayed work
dominance_rules.action: compact/externalize or refuse; never silent truncate

dominance_rules.rationale: lost safety/scope rules beat lost chatter
dominance_rules.action: protect pins; drop duplicates and aged L2 first

dominance_rules.rationale: high compression with failed probes is a defect
dominance_rules.trigger: ratio targets conflict with probe scores
dominance_rules.action: stop at floor; keep more narrative

dominance_rules.rationale: next action needs goal/paths more than old acks
FIFO drops system and early acceptance criteria
dominance_rules.action: ordered eviction; emergency window only with re-pin

dominance_rules.rationale: N full clones exhaust budgets and leak irrelevancies

dominance_rules.action: repo/store paths with hash; no bare /tmp

iteration_protocol.action: ordered eviction + externalize; re-pin; retry once; else refuse
restore pins from register; reduce compression; re-place positions
update p90 priors; force externalize path for that tool
strengthen L0/register; extend working set; check eviction logs
shrink packet; remove parent history; raise worker-side compact
fix locators; migrate ephemeral to durable store
raise util threshold; set min turns between compacts

priority_rationale: Token metering, invariants, and working set outrank digest polish; enforcement and eviction safety outrank aggressive compression ratios.
